events.description: CIA issued an information report, not finally evaluated, to the White House and other agencies. The report states that a hijacking operation in the United States was stalled after confirmation of the arrest of two persons involved. The rest of the text is excised.

CIA issued an unevaluated intelligence information report, disseminated to the White House Situation Room, State, DIA, NSA, Secret Service, FBI, DOJ, DOT and FAA, saying a hijacking operation in the US was stalled.

Arrest of two persons involved in a planned hijacking operation in the United States was confirmed; the operation was reported stalled as a result. The persons' names are redacted and the exact date is not given.

sources_cited: CIA information report dated 8 January 1999 (heavily redacted; source excised)
key_claims: A CIA report of 8 January 1999 says a hijacking operation in the United States was stalled after confirmation that two people involved had been arrested.
The title indicates the report claims Bin Ladin postponed the hijacking, but the text in this chunk does not name him because of redaction.
The report was distributed to the White House Situation Room, State, DIA, NSA, FBI, FAA, DOT and other agencies.
The report is marked as an information report, not finally evaluated intelligence.
